Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Grand Junction CO
1110 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Snow is moving in along the northern and central Divide
  overnight with the heaviest snow falling through the morning
  and early afternoon. Snow totals of 10-15 inches are expected
  for the Park and Elkhead mountains, with 4-8 inches across 
  the Flat Tops and Central Divide Mountains.

- Winds gusting 40 to 50 mph are expected with this system  
  through Saturday night, leading to blowing and drifting snow 
  and difficult driving conditions over the mountain passes.

- An unsettled pattern looks to continue into next week with
  potential for more mountain snow by mid week, but details 
  remain uncertain.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1102 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

The winter storm forecast for tonight and tomorrow is on track with 
little change. Light snow is falling on the Park Range with an inch 
accumulation so far, and light snow is falling on I-70 over Vail 
Pass. The Winter Storm Warning is still in effect for the Park and 
Elkhead Mountains through 5 AM Sunday for 10 to 15 inches new snow 
with locally higher amounts possible. Likewise, the Winter Weather 
Advisories for the Flat Tops, and Gore and Elk Mountains including 
the I-70 mountain corridor through Vail and Vail Pass also remains 
in effect for the same period for four to eight inches new snow with 
locally higher amounts possible. This system has plenty of moisture 
available from the atmospheric river (AR) impacting Oregon, and the 
shortwave dropping down from the Pacific Northwest in the morning 
has strong upper-level dynamics from the left exit region of the jet 
moving overhead. Look for the heaviest snowfall over the mountains 
between about 8 AM and 2 PM and we could see a periods with snow 
squalls as the shortwave passes. Snow squalls can produce heavy snow 
and strong winds leading to near zero visibilities in the snow and 
blowing snow along with roads flash freezing, quickly becoming 
treacherous. If you are on the road and receive a warning for a snow 
squall, best practices are to find a location where you can safely 
pull off and wait out the storm. They typically pass quickly in 10 
to 20 minutes, and then you can continue your travel as road 
conditions permit. 

The 00Z models are just coming in now and are indicating the jet 
streak dipping farther south that the previous model runs have 
suggested. Will need to watch this overnight as it could push the 
snow band farther south and west bringing impacts to the Tavaputs, 
Grand Mesa and the Uncompahgre Plateau. Stay tuned for updates on 
this as there could be some big changes. 

SUNDAY AND BEYOND:

The transitory ridge moves in from the west Sunday morning to push 
the showers on east out of eastern Utah and Western Colorado. but a 
few orographic showers may continue through the day along the divide 
from lingering moisture. A weak system passes to the north Monday 
bringing only a slight, less than 25% chance of showers to the 
northern mountains with little if any accumulation. The next system 
to impact the region comes in Tuesday night into Thursday. It has a 
tap on moisture from an AR moving in through the LA Basin and will 
have the most significant impacts on the southern face of the San 
Juan Mountains. It's too early to say significant this system will 
be as the models very significantly from run to run. The latest run 
has tracked the low farther north over the Four Corners which would 
bring a much more impactful storm, but confidence is low at this 
point. Stay tuned for updates on this system through the weekend. By 
Monday we should have a much better handle on this one.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 1109 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

High clouds have moved in this evening with some midlevel 
ceilings also being reported across the area. KASE, KEGE and 
KHDN are reporting overcast skies around 5K feet and expect 
they'll be dropping to MVFR/IFR through the day as lower 
ceilings and showers move through. KRIL, KGUC and KTEX are also 
expected to see some light precip through the day which may drop
conditions to MVFR from time to time. Some gusty winds of 20 to
30 kts are also possible for TAf sites. Those same TAF sites 
mentioned above will also likely remain below ILS breakpoints 
through the day.

&&
